## K16 · K16-limits — K16: how far the kernel's fixed limits rise, and what each costs

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 9

Evidence: Owner's values (two decision_requests on this thread): MAX_PROCESS_COUNT 512 with 16-bit PIDs; threads with a context allocated per thread, 255; MAX_OPEN_CALLS 256, MAX_DEPTH 16, MAX_LABELS 16, WAIT_CAP 32, MAX_START_HANDLES 128. Architect's design in the brief .wash/local/K16-implementer.md: Pid NonZeroU16 with the ASID out of satp; every walk visits only live threads first and is measured against GATE1's numbers; a thread's saved registers live in its IPC page so a context costs no page of its own and static memory no longer grows with T; PROCESS_AREA one page on both widths with a TID-to-frame table the trap entry indexes; per-PID tables in .bss (~375 KB per width at 512) with a 64 KiB headroom stop; no N-sized arrays on the kernel stack; the pages move in K16's commits. K16 needs GATE1, INIT1, K13.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `4cfd23b12c32a230f92f70e2d71b8b2b` · 2026-10-02T07:19:59Z

> Designed; brief .wash/local/K16-implementer.md; plan node K16 updated (needs GATE1, INIT1, K13, this thread). Values go to the owner now (decision_request on this thread); I recommend N 253, T 63, MAX_OPEN_CALLS 256, MAX_DEPTH 16, MAX_LABELS 16, WAIT_CAP and MAX_START_HANDLES unchanged. Ruled (tenet 1, the pages):
> 1. Tables stay static. Measured N=253,T=63: rv32 .data 83->276 KB (512 KiB region), rv32 image 218->412 KB of link.x's 512 KiB FLASH; rv64 .data 89->286 KB. ~850 B/PID.
> 2. 256 is out without widening Pid: PID is NonZeroU8, 254/255 are DMA_OWNER/OBJECT_OWNER; 253 keeps every table, the loader handoff and Sv32's 9-bit ASID as they are.
> 3. T=63 is a u64 mask; widen allocated_threads (u32) and ProcessState::Ready/Running (usize, 32-bit on rv32). ProcessImpl 2 pages rv32 / 4 rv64, charged per process. 127 would hit rv32's EXIT_THREAD at PROCESS_AREA+0x3000. Handle frame index, dma_mapped, notice PID: unaffected.
> 4. N x T walks go 1,984 -> 15,939 slots. A pump is ~1.2 ms at the gate fill; by slot that's ~8x and breaks R10's 30 ms. Ruling: walks visit only existing processes and threads with an IPC page (a u64 TID mask in Account), so cost follows live threads. Commit 1 lands that with values unchanged and remeasures; then the values; then the gate and sched-latency rerun at the new values on both widths in K16 itself, plus a process-fill case (PIDs 2..=253) and a measured worst walk (all threads live) as a stated residual.
> 5. Needs: K13 (message.rs holds every walk), INIT1 (boot_*, setup_loader_process, the loader's context mapping, boot.md's 63), GATE1 (its numbers are the baseline). No page changes before the code: today's limits are current behaviour.

### Architect · Owner decision requested

Event: `27a3f63af5cc0bcc36e0e51159ec0923` · 2026-10-02T07:20:06Z

> K16: how far the kernel's limits rise
> 
> 1. MAX_PROCESS_COUNT is 64. The PID is one byte (254 and 255 are reserved frame owners), so 253 is the most without widening it. Static kernel memory grows ~850 B per PID (rv32 image 218 KB -> ~412 KB of its 512 KiB at 253). Which?
>    - 253 (recommended): The byte's ceiling; no format changes. PIDs 2..=253.
>    - 128: Half the static cost and walk length; rv32 image ~280 KB.
>    - 512+ with 16-bit PIDs: Widens Pid: the loader's and kernel's frame ownership tables double, the boot handoff changes; Sv32's 9-bit ASID caps at 511.
> 2. MAX_THREADS is 31 (a 32-bit mask, TID 0 unused). Every process pays its saved contexts whether it uses them or not. Which?
>    - 63 (recommended): u64 masks on both widths; contexts 2 pages a process on rv32, 4 on rv64 (from 1 and 2). beamlet's waiting threads 22 -> 54.
>    - 127: u128 masks; 4 pages rv32, 8 on rv64 per process; rv32's magic return address must move.
>    - Keep 31: No change.
> 3. The per-object caps. Which set?
>    - Recommended set (recommended): MAX_OPEN_CALLS 64->256 (a shared server can park only 48 calls box-wide today); MAX_DEPTH 8->16 (the lease chain already uses 7 levels); MAX_LABELS 8->16 (ABI records grow 8 slots); WAIT_CAP 16 and MAX_START_HANDLES 64 unchanged (a burst limit and a stack array, nothing grows into them).
>    - Recommended set, plus WAIT_CAP 32 and MAX_START_HANDLES 128: Raise all five.
>    - Only processes and threads now: Leave every per-object cap as it is.

Event: `fcdda68148e2c5a6e2aea6ccbabe3ab2` · 2026-10-02T07:29:06Z

> The owner chose 16-bit PIDs, 512+ processes, and skipped threads and the caps. Those two and the exact count go back to the owner now. Ruled for 16-bit PIDs (brief updated; K16 is now Tier A kernel+loader, size L, same needs):
> 6. Pid becomes NonZeroU16 in libs/layout, so the loader's and kernel's ownership tables are 2 B a frame. OBJECT_OWNER/DMA_OWNER become 0xffff/0xfffe.
> 7. satp drops the PID: Sv32's ASID is 9 bits, and every switch already flushes the whole TLB. ASID is 0; current_pid is the only record; satp_pid, pid_from_satp and the satp check go; the loader's handoff record gets a PID field. memory-layout.md's satp section is rewritten. ASIDs for several harts are M2's.
> 1 (revised). At N=512 the per-PID tables are about 530 KB on each width, past both link scripts' 512 KiB RAM region (1.05 MB at 1024). So the tables' empty value is all zeros (.bss, so the image doesn't grow), and the kernel data region grows to 1.5 MiB on both widths (rv32 0xffd8_0000..0xfff0_0000). No N-sized array on the 32 KiB kernel stack: sched.rs runnable is 8 KiB at 512.
> 8. The stride queue scans N slots on every pick; sched-latency measures it at the new N.
> Commits: walks by live thread -> 16-bit PIDs/satp -> data region -> values -> process-fill, worst walk, depth 16.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `b5092e6b8aad226afa18ca52a291955c` · 2026-10-02T07:42:02Z

> Owner's values are in: N 512 (16-bit PIDs); T "context allocated per thread, 255+"; caps: MAX_OPEN_CALLS 256, MAX_DEPTH 16, MAX_LABELS 16, WAIT_CAP 32, MAX_START_HANDLES 128. Design is complete; brief rewritten at .wash/local/K16-implementer.md; plan node body updated (same needs: GATE1, INIT1, K13; Tier A kernel+loader, size L).
> Rulings for threads:
> - T = 255. A TID stays a byte, masks are [u64;4], and 255 meets "255+". More would outgrow the header page's TID table and the masks.
> - A thread's saved registers move into its IPC page, which every thread already has and pays for (one page). 297 + 32 words of 512. A process pays for the threads it has; a context costs no page of its own.
> - PROCESS_AREA becomes one page on both widths: the header, a no-thread context, and the TID->IPC-frame table. The trap entry loads the context's address from header slot 1 instead of shifting a number. Account::ipc (static) goes, so static memory no longer grows with T. rv64 processes save 1 page each.
> - Walk slots go 1,984 -> 130,560. Walks by live thread are mandatory (commit 1, measured against GATE1's numbers).
> - Static at 512 is ~375 KB/width; the tables go to .bss and the image doesn't grow. The 512 KiB data region holds them; if the headroom drops under 64 KiB, the implementer stops and I grow it.
> - No N- or 128-sized array is duplicated on the kernel stack (sched runnable; process_start's two decode arrays become one).
> No page changes before the code: the limits are current behaviour, and the pages move in K16's commits. The thread can be resolved with the brief as evidence.
